# Skeleton

Skeleton is a component of `@kozmos-ds/react` whose docs do not describe it yet.

- **Import:** `import { Skeleton } from "@kozmos-ds/react";`
- **Group:** Feedback
- **Platforms:** React, SwiftUI and Compose; linked to its Figma component through Code Connect.
- **Storybook:** <https://vodoco.github.io/kozmos-design-system/storybook/?path=/docs/feedback-skeleton--docs>

## Example

From its `Default` story.

```tsx
import { Skeleton, ThemeProvider } from "@kozmos-ds/react";

export function SkeletonExample() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="light">
      <div className="flex w-full items-center gap-4" style={{ maxWidth: 320 }}>
        <Skeleton className="h-12 w-12 shrink-0 rounded-pill" />
        <div className="min-w-0 flex-1 space-y-2">
          <Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />
          <Skeleton className="h-4 w-3/4" />
        </div>
      </div>
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

## Skeleton

It forwards its ref to `HTMLDivElement`. Its props are `SkeletonProps`, which extends `React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>`.

- `shape`: `SkeletonShape`, optional.
- `width`: `number | string`, optional.

  The space to hold. A number is pixels; a string is any CSS length, so a
  placeholder can be `"60%"` of its row.

  These exist so a loading state needs no inline style of its own — which
  was the whole of GAP-057. A circle takes `width` as its diameter and needs
  nothing else.

- `height`: `number | string`, optional.
- `children`: `ReactNode`, optional.

It also takes the 263 attributes React's DOM types give it (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, the event handlers among them).

## Types these props take

### SkeletonShape

From `@kozmos-ds/react`.

```ts
/**
 * What the placeholder stands in for, which is all that decides its shape.
 *
 * `line` is a row of text; `block` a card, a media tile, a panel; `circle` an
 * avatar or a round icon button. The three match the Figma set's `Shape` axis,
 * so a loading state drawn in one place reads the same in the other.
 */
type SkeletonShape = "line" | "block" | "circle";
```
